design.selected: Private case ledger, independent delivery/judgment partitions and family-derived RunResults; direct public comparison summaries and three fixed encoders.
design.reason: Keeps one count-policy owner and a small public interface without a generic report document framework.
reconciliations: Selected families are seeded from pinned checks even if unrun.
Unordered check content compatibility is distinct from ordered execution input differences.
Detailed RunResults leaves the existing RunSummary history item unchanged.
New coherent read_runs supplies capture labels while read_run keeps existing capture/equality behavior.

scope_limits: Deterministic loopback provider replies do not establish hosted Groq or semantic assessment accuracy.
No numerical deltas, paired-input claims or combined security score.
Historical planned case counts and immutable remote revisions are unknown.
Atomic visibility is proved on local WSL/native Windows filesystems, not hostile ancestor mutation or Windows power-loss durability.
Physical terminal acceptance and live hosted providers remain Task 10.

Base is B, the private case ledger with orthogonal delivery and judgment partitions and family-derived totals. Parent agrees with that caller gap and accepts C's useful public-compare requirement, but resolves it by returning typed RunResults values beside views and assessment. A document/node/reference vocabulary is unnecessary for three fixed formats once all consumers use the same summary. No renderer computes counts.

Parent scores before grafts against six rubric criteria: A [2,3,2,2,2,3]=14; B [3,3,2,3,2,2]=15; C [2,3,2,3,2,3]=15. Parent weights B's explicit disjoint counts and minimal API over C's complete but larger public layout shape. The C caller gap is eliminated by one summary field, raising B interface/proof scores to3 each (17/18). Both designs still require actual filesystem proof rather than a paper score3. This is a deliberate disagreement on base choice, with the substantive gap accepted rather than dismissed. Independent implementation/code/security review must test the accepted contract, including direct compare counts.

## Caller and data shape

Commands: compare ID ID [ID...] and report ID [ID...] --format {json,markdown,html} --output PATH [--overwrite]. Report always writes a file and emits the existing JSON-compatible receipt. Compare succeeds as inspection even when assessment is incompatible, and immediately exposes counts/denominators. Finding show adds coherent context while preserving original Finding fields at their old JSON locations; finding list keeps current UUID cursor/page contract.

Use B's RunResults with requested/generated checks, planned_cases null, per-family attack/control verdict partitions seeded from every requested pinned check, independent per-kind DeliveryCounts, nullable usage coverage, evaluator actor counts, stage status/error diagnostics and truncation/redaction. Overall counts derive from family records. Private _Case joins raw immutable evidence once. Public Comparison retains source runs, adds their typed summaries in the same order plus structured assessment; preserve old compatible/differences as derived projections. Summary includes run identity so correspondence is explicit; compare constructs the paired values once and validates ordering/identities. No duplicate counting policy. render_report(Comparison) consumes those summaries; single RunView is summarized once. Serializable count contracts can live in domain.py to keep its Comparison dependency acyclic; results.py owns interpretation.

Graft A's actionable corruption guard: reject duplicate or impossible required lineage rather than overwriting maps. Ordinary optional historical fields remain valid missing/unknown evidence, never corruption merely for being absent. Planned case policy is unknown for existing snapshots. Delivery and judgment are independent partitions; no technical error becomes an invented verdict. No percentages or combined score are needed. Metadata/evidence remain authoritative in source RunViews and full JSON, with readable summary/identity/usage/evidence sections in Markdown/HTML.

Comparison assessment same_pinned_settings / cross_model / incompatible. Compare complete check content ignoring order for checks_compatible, but record any ordered check-ID sequence change as an execution mismatch that prevents same_pinned_settings or cross_model. The Selector receives checks in snapshot order, so reordered checks are a known changed input. Compare all evaluator configs and prompts, and target execution config/limits excluding profile UUID/name. Only a target-model change with all other compared settings equal yields cross_model. compatible is a conservative projection of same_pinned_settings, not a remote-equivalence assertion. All assessments explicitly keep remote_revision unknown and generated input matching not_established. Never claim like-for-like, causality, paired deltas or a ranking. Seed family rows from pinned requested checks, even when generated cases are zero. A selected-but-unrun family has requested_checks>0, generated=0 and missing coverage. Only a family absent from that run snapshot is not-selected. Never infer selection from generated cases. Show side-by-side counts for every relation with its label.

## Coherent capture and legacy reads

Repository.read_runs(ids) performs all _view calls in one existing read transaction and preserves caller order; missing ID fails the whole read. New optional RunView.captured_at defaults None. Populate it only for the new read_runs API, including one-ID report reads, with one shared UTC capture label. pstack skills are written in Claude Code tool language (the `Skill` tool, the `Agent` tool, `AskUserQuestion`, Claude model names). On Codex the skills are the same files; only the tool names resolve differently. Read this when a pstack skill names a Claude tool, a driver or bundled skill, or a Claude model. This file is Codex-specific. Gemini CLI, opencode, Prime Agent, and other runtimes must use their own concrete tools, model names, and configuration paths.

## Tool actions

| pstack / Claude action | Codex equivalent |
|------------------------|------------------|
| Read a file | `shell` (`cat`, `head`, `tail`) |
| Create / edit / delete a file | `apply_patch` |
| Run a shell command | `shell` |
| Search file contents / find files | `shell` (`rg`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`) |
| Fetch a URL | `shell` with `curl` / `wget` |
| Search the web | `web_search` |
| Invoke a skill (the `Skill` tool, `/command`) | Skills load natively. Follow the instructions presented. |
| Dispatch a subagent (the `Agent`/`Task` tool) | `spawn_agent` |
| Dispatch N parallel subagents in one turn | N `spawn_agent` calls in one response |
| Wait for a subagent result | `wait_agent` |
| Free a finished subagent slot | `close_agent`, when the session exposes it. Some Codex hosts don't. |
| Track tasks (the todolist; `TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate`, or `TodoWrite` on Claude Code) | `update_plan` |
| Ask the human a fixed-choice question (`AskUserQuestion`) | Ask in plain text and let the user answer. Codex has no structured-choice tool. |

Subagent dispatch needs `multi_agent` enabled. Add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[features]
multi_agent = true
```

Without it, `spawn_agent` is unavailable and the fan-out skills (`interrogate`, `why`, `how`, `arena`, `reflect`) degrade to a single sequential pass. A required independent review does not degrade. It stays blocked, as poteto-mode's [Subagents](../SKILL.md#subagents) section says.

Enabling `multi_agent` does not lift the host's thread limit. A thread-limit error from `spawn_agent` is a capacity error, not a rejected model slug, so the skills' fallback to another model does not apply. After the first capacity rejection, stop spawning. Close a finished agent with `close_agent` before you try again, and where the session has no `close_agent`, do not assume a finished agent's slot is free.

## Subagent policy

poteto-mode's Subagents section sets Claude-specific defaults (`subagent_type: "pstack:poteto-agent"`, `run_in_background: true`). On Codex:

- There is no `poteto-agent` subagent type. Route an ad-hoc subagent through poteto-mode's style by dispatching a `spawn_agent` whose instructions tell it to read the `poteto-mode` skill in full first.
- `spawn_agent` calls already run concurrently with your turn, so `run_in_background: true` has no separate flag. Issue the dispatch and continue.
- There are no `pstack:effort-<level>` or `pstack:poteto-agent-<level>` types. When a role value carries `@<level>`, or the `default effort` line names a level, pass that level as `spawn_agent`'s `reasoning_effort` and keep the dispatch otherwise unchanged. `session` passes no `reasoning_effort`.
- There is no `comment-sicko` subagent type either. The **no-comments** skill spawns it on Claude Code; on Codex dispatch a `spawn_agent` whose instructions tell it to read `poteto-mode/references/agents/comment-sicko.md` in full first.
- Claude Code runs every subagent on this machine, so the **swarm** skill's workers and the fan-out playbooks (`orchestrate`, `autopilot-full`, `autopilot-stack`) isolate writers with worktrees. The same holds on Codex.
- Keep the rest of the policy unchanged. Pass file pointers not inlined context, give each worker its own worktree or branch when they write, review every subagent's diff yourself.

## Model names

Skills name Claude defaults (a single-role default for code/prose/judgment plus a diverse-model panel for diverse-model panels; each model-consuming skill lists its own in a Models section). These slugs do not resolve on Codex. Substitute your configured Codex models:

- Single-model roles: your primary Codex model (for example `gpt-6-sol`).
- Roles that default to the strongest Claude model (`bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, `hillclimb`, `strongest judgment`): your strongest Codex model (for example `gpt-6-astra`).
- Diverse-model panels (`arena`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `how` critics, `reflect`): the adversarial signal comes from model diversity, so use the distinct Codex models available to you. A good default panel on ChatGPT is `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`. If only one model family is reachable, vary reasoning effort and note in the verdict that diversity was reduced.

`/setup-pstack` writes the configured model list. On Codex, set it to your Codex model slugs.

## Session routing hook

The native pstack plugin bundles the same `SessionStart` routing instruction as the Claude Code plugin, through `session-start.sh` on macOS and Linux and `session-start.ps1` on Windows. Codex runs the hook on startup, resume, clear, and compact after the user trusts the hook through `/hooks`. The hook reads `session hook` from the Codex sheet, at the path in [setup-pstack's runtime table](../../setup-pstack/SKILL.md#other-runtimes); `session hook: off` disables injection.

A skills-only installation does not include plugin hooks. Request `poteto-mode` explicitly or add a standing instruction to `AGENTS.md` in that case.

The [driver policy](../SKILL.md#non-negotiables) selects the app driver. For skills and drivers named by these workflows, use these Codex equivalents:

## Vendored scripts

`skills/poteto-mode/scripts/` ships the `watch-pr` PR watcher, the `orch` store CLI, and `worktree-audit.mjs`. The `watch-pr/ship-pr` command owns pending-merge inspection and cancellation; `resume.mjs` owns the shared checkpoint locator described in [Resume storage](resume-storage.md). These scripts use bun and Node.js and run the same on Codex; invoke them through `shell`. They need `bun`, `gh`, and (for stack work) `gt`. Run `worktree-audit.mjs` with `node`, as its shebang does. The audit follows each link in a worktree's ancestor directories with `stat` and matches it by the directory it lands on, under bun and node alike. A worktree whose own path bun cannot resolve loses its last chat and lands in `review`. A dangling or looping link is ignored. Any other link that `stat` cannot follow puts every worktree under the link's directory in `review`, with a warning that names the link. `worktree-audit.mjs` scans Codex sessions under `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` and `$CODEX_HOME/archived_sessions` (default `~/.codex`), along with any Claude Code or Pi transcript directory that exists. It imports the transcript walker from `skills/reflect/scripts/find-transcript.mjs`, so keep the `reflect` skill installed beside `poteto-mode`.

# Task 9 candidate A: case ledger with pure projections

## Problem

Saved `RunView` already contains pinned inputs and most observed lineage, while findings pages and single-run reads already work. Reporting must interpret partial evidence without treating missing work as a pass, target and evaluator requests as one population, or locally equal model names as proof of equal remote revisions. A comparison additionally needs all runs from one SQLite read transaction. Exporting those interpretations must be safe for hostile saved text and concurrent local writers. The core design is one **case ledger** per view, projected into summaries and formats, with repository reads and filesystem publication at the outer edges.

## Usage (caller's view)

```console
asclepius findings list --run RUN_ID --limit 50
asclepius findings show FINDING_ID
asclepius compare RUN_A RUN_B --json
asclepius report RUN_ID --format html --output ./reports/run.html
asclepius report --compare RUN_A RUN_B --format markdown --output ./reports/side-by-side.md
asclepius report RUN_ID --format json                  # stdout, existing JSON envelope
asclepius report RUN_ID --format html --output ./reports/run.html --overwrite
```

`--output` is mandatory for HTML and Markdown and optional for JSON; without output, JSON uses the existing `--json` envelope. With output, success emits a small path/format receipt through existing `emit`, never the entire artifact. Argument errors keep exit 2, missing IDs exit 3, and storage/export errors use the existing AppError path. CLI controls formatting; results code never touches stdout.

```python
# A saved run can be inspected with the daemon stopped.
view = await repo.read_run(run_id)
artifact = render_report(view, "html")
path = write_export(artifact, Path("reports/run.html"))

# All comparison inputs are captured together; callers do not gather read_run calls.
comparison = await compare_runs(repo, [run_a, run_b])
assert comparison.relation in {"same_local_configuration", "cross_model", "descriptive_only"}
artifact = render_report(comparison, "markdown")

# Detail is a coherent lineage, while existing list pagination stays Page[Finding].
detail = await repo.read_finding_detail(finding_id)
print(safe_terminal(detail.finding.description))
```

## Shape

The case ledger is private to `results.py`. It is built once from a `RunView` and gives each generated variant exactly one row. The row joins by IDs to at most one target observation, judgment, and finding; malformed or duplicate persisted lineage is an explicit data-integrity error, never silently counted twice. Non-target observations go into a separate actor aggregate. A zero-generated run produces an empty case tuple with `denominator=0` and null rates. The snapshot still has at least one check.

Requested checks and generated cases are separate figures. The current executor's three attacks plus one control per selected check is a code policy, not a historical field in `RunSnapshot`; the report therefore leaves planned case counts unknown unless a future persisted policy field proves them. It never computes `4 × checks` for arbitrary saved runs. A completed run with zero findings means zero saved findings, not zero weaknesses or a successful attack rate.

```python
# domain.py additions. Names show intended immutable Pydantic contract shape.
class CountFraction(Contract):
    count: NonNegativeInt
    denominator: NonNegativeInt
    rate: float | None                 # null iff denominator is zero or coverage is insufficient

class AttackCounts(Contract):
    generated: NonNegativeInt
    unobserved: NonNegativeInt
    transport_error: NonNegativeInt
    unknown_observation: NonNegativeInt
    successful_reply_unjudged: NonNegativeInt
    weakness: NonNegativeInt
    pass_count: NonNegativeInt
    inconclusive: NonNegativeInt
    verdict_missing: NonNegativeInt
    judge_attempts: AttemptCounts    # separate diagnostic, not a generated-case bucket

class ControlCounts(Contract):
    generated: NonNegativeInt
    unobserved: NonNegativeInt
    transport_error: NonNegativeInt
    unknown_observation: NonNegativeInt
    successful_reply_unjudged: NonNegativeInt
    answered: NonNegativeInt
    over_refusal: NonNegativeInt
    inconclusive: NonNegativeInt
    outcome_missing: NonNegativeInt
    judge_attempts: AttemptCounts

class UsageTotal(Contract):
    input_tokens: NonNegativeInt | None
    output_tokens: NonNegativeInt | None
    input_covered: NonNegativeInt
    output_covered: NonNegativeInt
    successful_observations: NonNegativeInt

class RunResults(Contract):
    run_id: UUID
    state: RunState
    reason: str | None
    as_of: UtcTime | None                # transaction read time or unknown for bare RunView
    checks_requested: NonNegativeInt
    generated_attacks: NonNegativeInt
    generated_controls: NonNegativeInt
    attack: AttackCounts
    control: ControlCounts               # project control outcome, not security verdict
    families: tuple[FamilyResults, ...]  # ordered by pinned check identity
    target_usage: UsageTotal
    evaluator_usage: UsageTotal
    evaluator_requests: ActorCounts      # selector/generator/judge/reporter only
    truncated_replies: NonNegativeInt
    redacted_replies: NonNegativeInt
    metadata: ReportMetadata             # pinned target/evaluator/prompt/check identities, limits
    limitations: tuple[str, ...]

class Comparison(Contract):
    schema_version: Literal[1] = 1
    runs: Annotated[tuple[RunView, ...], Field(min_length=2)]  # preserve existing field
    compatible: bool                    # true only for the first two relation values below
    differences: tuple[str, ...] = ()   # preserve existing field, deterministic explanations
    relation: Literal["same_local_configuration", "cross_model", "descriptive_only"]
    check_compatible: bool
    results: tuple[RunResults, ...]
    remote_revision: Literal["unknown"] = "unknown"
    inputs_paired: bool = False          # no evidence of paired generated attacks

class FindingDetail(Contract):
    finding: Finding
    check: CheckDefinition
    variant: Variant
    observation: Observation | None
    judgment: Judgment
    # All saved evidence remains visible via the constituent domain records.
```

The case buckets in each kind sum to its generated count. `AttemptCounts` is an independent diagnostic breakdown of persisted Judge attempts, not an additional case bucket. A judgment after a target error is inconsistent lineage and raises a data-integrity error. Existing `Judgment.security_verdict=None` stays separate from `inconclusive`. Findings are reported as their own count over weakness judgments, not as a verdict bucket: a Reporter failure may leave a weakness with no Finding. Likewise diagnostic assertions and metrics retain their own saved denominators and are listed separately, never averaged into a security score.

`RunResults` should include named budget limits and observed usage coverage, including independently unknown token counters. No billed-cost estimate is added. The pinned metadata must include check versions and full check-content digest; target provider, base URL, model, system prompt, settings and capability digest; all four evaluator role configurations and prompt versions/content digests; local credential-reference identity with a note that it does not prove secret/account sameness. The report retains raw byte count, truncation and redaction indications beside evidence. `as_of` comes from the same repository transaction that materializes the view; for a directly supplied historical `RunView` lacking read metadata, `render_report` labels capture time `unknown` rather than inventing the current time.

The public surface stays small:

```python
# storage.py; one transaction, ordered exactly as requested; duplicate IDs rejected at boundary.
async def read_runs(self, run_ids: Sequence[UUID]) -> tuple[RunView, ...]: ...
async def read_finding_detail(self, finding_id: UUID) -> FindingDetail: ...

# results.py; pure projection after one coherent read.
async def compare_runs(repo: Repository, run_ids: list[str]) -> Comparison: ...
def summarize_run(view: RunView, *, as_of: datetime | None = None) -> RunResults: ...

# exports.py; no repository, adapter, service, or daemon dependency.
def render_report(view: RunView | Comparison, format: str) -> ExportArtifact: ...
def write_export(artifact: ExportArtifact, destination: Path, overwrite: bool = False) -> Path: ...
def safe_terminal(text: str) -> str: ...
```

`read_runs` validates IDs and resolves every `_view` in one `_run` transaction; any missing ID fails the whole request. The repository can expose a `ReadCapture` containing `captured_at` and views instead of bare views if adding time metadata earns its cost. It does not expose SQL rows or operation wires. A separate exact intent read is unnecessary because the report says `generated but unobserved` rather than claiming exact in-flight dispatches. Stage attempts are shown as persisted attempts, never reconstructed intent counts. `read_finding_detail` joins Finding, Variant, pinned Check, target Observation and Judgment in one transaction. Existing `read_finding` and `list_findings` remain valid; list retains UUID cursor order and its per-page snapshot caveat.

Comparison computes **three independent judgments**. Pinned checks are equal only when their complete canonical content (including rubric, assertions, severity, strategies, controls and versions) is equal independent of order. Evaluator identity compares all four role configurations and prompt content. Target identity compares provider, endpoint, system prompt, generation settings, capabilities, limits and credential reference separately from model. `same_local_configuration` requires all pinned local execution config equal. `cross_model` permits exactly a changed target model with equal checks, evaluator and other target settings. Everything else is `descriptive_only` with explicit changed/unknown fields. Even in the first relation, remote application/model revision is unknown; local equality is never called true like-for-like execution. No outcome delta is computed. The comparison presents side-by-side per-run counts and denominators, per-family rows, missingness and state. It says generated attack inputs may differ, so the rows are unpaired. `compatible` means the side-by-side result belongs to the first two relation classes, not that causal numerical deltas are safe. A live/partial run retains its relation label but prominently marks outcome coverage incomplete. A snapshot that cannot establish a required identity is `descriptive_only` with a reason, never implicitly equal.

The four formats use one `RunResults`/`Comparison` projection. JSON serializes typed data with explicit nulls and stable schema. Markdown emits fixed headings and table cells with all untrusted text escaped for pipes, brackets, parentheses, backticks, angle brackets and line breaks; long arbitrary prompts/replies/evidence appear as escaped text blocks, never fenced code or link syntax. HTML uses fixed elements only, text and every attribute escaped, no `script`, link, form, external font/resource or active URL. SVG uses fixed local geometry and numeric counts from validated integers, with accessible text labels; no untrusted string enters raw SVG markup. Family names are escaped text. Zero denominators show `N/A (0 generated)` instead of a percentage. All formats say whether the run is live/partial and show coverage, unknown fields, errors, uncertainty and source identity. `safe_terminal` replaces C0/C1 controls, ESC, DEL, bidi controls and OSC-containing sequences with visible escaped code points; it is applied at terminal output and human error boundaries, including malicious destination labels. JSON retains original strings under JSON escaping.

The export writer first validates a regular local destination directory and destination path. It acquires a persistent sibling lock file for that destination (portalocker; lock file never unlinked), writes a uniquely named private temporary regular file in the same directory, flushes and `fsync`s it, and commits once. With `overwrite=False`, atomic hard-link creation from temp to destination is the no-clobber publication primitive; `FileExistsError` refuses even a noncooperating concurrent creator. With `overwrite=True`, reject an existing symlink or multiply linked destination and use `os.replace` to replace only the directory entry; the old file remains complete until commit. Reject symlinks for the destination directory and destination entry under the lock. `fsync` the parent directory where supported, then remove only this invocation's temp. A crash after hard-link publication may leave an orphan temp but the destination is complete. A crash before publication leaves the previous destination complete. These guarantees assume a trusted local filesystem supporting same-directory hard links and atomic rename/replace; unsupported filesystems fail explicitly instead of falling back to a check-then-write race. A noncooperating actor able to swap entries during overwrite or tamper with the directory is outside that trusted-directory assumption. Lock names are derived from the destination basename and held through commit; lock paths are persistent to avoid unlink races.

Pseudocode for the central projection:

```python
def summarize_run(view, *, as_of=None):
    # TODO: index variants, target observations, judgments and findings by their stable IDs.
    # TODO: reject duplicate/impossible lineage, then emit one disjoint row per variant.
    # TODO: fold attack and control rows separately; fold non-target observations by actor.
    # TODO: retain missing usage coverage and evidence limits; derive family rows from checks.
    # TODO: return typed results with null rates when denominator or coverage forbids a rate.
    raise NotImplementedError

async def compare_runs(repo, run_ids):
    # TODO: parse canonical IDs and read all views in one repository transaction.
    # TODO: classify complete pinned checks, evaluator config and target config separately.
    # TODO: attach per-run projections and deterministic mismatch/uncertainty reasons.
    raise NotImplementedError
```

`results.py` owns interpretation, `exports.py` owns serialization and publication, `storage.py` owns coherent reads, `domain.py` owns public contracts, and `cli.py` owns argument parsing plus terminal boundary. A reader follows CLI to repository/results to exporter in at most three modules for either report path. Validation occurs at CLI/repository/filesystem edges; the central projection is pure. This hides joins, coverage arithmetic, compatibility and safe rendering behind four requested functions. It leaves only the report format and destination choice with the caller.

## Synthesis decision

This independent candidate is available for arena synthesis. No other candidate was consulted.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept an internal case ledger and several explicit count types in exchange for one source of denominator truth across JSON, Markdown, HTML and comparison.
- We accept side-by-side counts without numerical deltas in exchange for honest treatment of unpaired generated inputs and unknown remote revisions.
- We accept an explicit failure on filesystems without atomic local link/replace guarantees in exchange for enforceable no-clobber and interruption behavior.
- We accept a read-time `unknown` label for an externally supplied `RunView` in exchange for not changing the established single-run read contract solely to stamp time.

## Alternatives considered

- A report-specific query layer with SQL aggregates would expose storage schema and divergent counting paths to format authors. It has a shallower implementation of each chart but a wider, harder-to-review interface.
- A generic report document/tree and templating framework would let each format share layout metadata, but it exposes a large renderer vocabulary and makes security rules harder to audit. Three fixed renderers over typed results have a deeper and smaller interface.
- Calling `read_run` for each ID and merging afterward would avoid a repository method, but exposes snapshot timing to every comparison caller and cannot promise coherent live comparisons.

## Implementation reconciliation

Not applicable to a design candidate. Accepted implementation deviations must update this usage and contract before a later unit relies on them.

## Open questions and risks

- Does `RunView` need a capture timestamp in its public contract, or is `unknown` enough for direct callers while the CLI uses a captured read wrapper? This design uses `unknown` unless a coherent repository timestamp is provided.
- Does the target deployment filesystem support hard links in the export directory on native Windows and WSL? The writer must prove the primitive with platform tests and fail clearly when unsupported.
- Are historical snapshots missing any pinned fields needed for strict equality? Those fields should force `descriptive_only` with an explicit unknown-field reason.

## Next implementation step

Add the coherent `Repository.read_runs` and `read_finding_detail` reads, then build the pure case-ledger projection against literal partial and complete saved fixtures.

design-b.md.content:
# Candidate B. Case-ledger reports over saved evidence

## Usage

A user can inspect a finding, compare saved runs, and export a report while the daemon is stopped. These commands require the existing store and never require provider credentials.

```sh
asclepius findings show FINDING_ID --json
asclepius compare RUN_A RUN_B --json
asclepius report RUN_A --format html --output report.html
asclepius report RUN_A RUN_B --format markdown --output comparison.md
```

`report` accepts one or more distinct run IDs, a required format, a required output path, and optional `--overwrite`. `compare` accepts at least two distinct run IDs. Comparison always displays evidence, even when settings differ. It labels the relation and suppresses numerical deltas. An incompatible comparison is a successful inspection, not an execution error.

Real call sites remain short.

```python
# cli.py, single run report
view = await repo.read_run(args.run_ids[0])
artifact = render_report(view, args.format)
path = write_export(artifact, args.output, overwrite=args.overwrite)
emit({"path": str(path), "format": artifact.format}, args.json)

# cli.py, multi-run report
comparison = await compare_runs(repo, args.run_ids)
path = write_export(render_report(comparison, args.format), args.output,
                    overwrite=args.overwrite)
emit({"path": str(path), "format": args.format}, args.json)

# cli.py, finding inspection
emit(await repo.read_finding_detail(args.finding_id), args.json)
```

The ordinary `compare` branch emits `await compare_runs(repo, ids)`. No CLI branch classifies outcomes, computes compatibility, escapes report content, or manages temporary files.

## Problem

Saved records already contain the evidence. Their relationships are the difficult part. Target HTTP observations, evaluator HTTP observations, generated cases, judgments, and findings count different things. A live snapshot can contain any committed prefix. Historical snapshots do not record an execution-policy version or exact planned case count. Equal saved settings also fail to establish equal remote revisions or identical generated attacks.

This design centers interpretation on one row per generated target case. All aggregate presentations derive from that ledger. It keeps raw evidence authoritative and avoids a parallel aggregate store or a generic document framework.

## Shape

### Data structures

Existing immutable Pydantic domain conventions apply. The following is a type sketch, not implementation. `NonNegativeInt`, existing domain records, and `Literal` have their normal meanings.

```python
# domain.py. Additive read metadata, no schema migration.
class RunView(FrozenModel):
    # Existing fields unchanged.
    captured_at: datetime | None = None
    # UTC time sampled when the repository pins its SQLite read snapshot.
    # None preserves old direct construction and serialized historical views.

class SettingDifference(FrozenModel):
    run_id: UUID
    scope: Literal["checks", "evaluator", "target", "limits"]
    field: str
    # Stable field path, never raw secret/config values in a diagnostic.

class ComparisonAssessment(FrozenModel):
    relation: Literal["same_pinned_settings", "cross_model", "incompatible"]
    checks_compatible: bool
    mismatches: tuple[SettingDifference, ...]
    remote_revision: Literal["unknown"] = "unknown"
    input_matching: Literal["not_established"] = "not_established"

class Comparison(FrozenModel):
    runs: tuple[RunView, ...]  # Existing >=2 validation retained.
    assessment: ComparisonAssessment
    # Existing compatible and differences remain serialized computed fields.
    # compatible means assessment.relation == "same_pinned_settings".
    # differences derives stable human text from assessment, never hand-synced.

class FindingDetail(Finding):
    captured_at: datetime
    variant: Variant
    check: CheckDefinition
    judgment: Judgment
    target_observation: Observation | None
    snapshot: RunSnapshot
    # Inherits all existing Finding fields at their original JSON locations.

# results.py. Ephemeral, private, frozen data. No storage representation.
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Case:
    variant: Variant
    check: CheckDefinition
    target: Observation | None
    judgment: Judgment | None
    finding: Finding | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Ledger:
    source: RunView
    cases: tuple[_Case, ...]
    # One transient join, then reductions. Evaluator observations remain in source.

class AttackCounts(FrozenModel):
    generated: NonNegativeInt
    weakness: NonNegativeInt
    passed: NonNegativeInt
    inconclusive: NonNegativeInt
    missing_judgment: NonNegativeInt
    missing_verdict: NonNegativeInt

class ControlCounts(FrozenModel):
    generated: NonNegativeInt
    answered: NonNegativeInt
    over_refusal: NonNegativeInt
    inconclusive: NonNegativeInt
    missing_judgment: NonNegativeInt
    missing_outcome: NonNegativeInt

class DeliveryCounts(FrozenModel):
    unobserved: NonNegativeInt
    success: NonNegativeInt
    transport_error: NonNegativeInt
    unknown: NonNegativeInt

class TokenTotal(FrozenModel):
    known_sum: NonNegativeInt | None
    known_observations: NonNegativeInt
    eligible_observations: NonNegativeInt
    # Eligible means successful observations in this actor scope.

class FamilyCounts(FrozenModel):
    family: str
    requested_checks: NonNegativeInt
    generated_checks: NonNegativeInt
    attacks: AttackCounts
    controls: ControlCounts
    attack_delivery: DeliveryCounts
    control_delivery: DeliveryCounts
    findings: NonNegativeInt

class RunSummary(FrozenModel):
    requested_checks: NonNegativeInt
    generated_checks: NonNegativeInt
    planned_cases: None  # No current persisted record establishes this count.
    families: tuple[FamilyCounts, ...]
    # Serialized computed fields sum families into overall attacks, controls,
    # delivery, findings. No separately stored totals.
    target_input_tokens: TokenTotal
    target_output_tokens: TokenTotal
    evaluator_input_tokens: TokenTotal
    evaluator_output_tokens: TokenTotal
    evaluator_observations_by_actor: dict[Actor, NonNegativeInt]
    stage_attempts_by_status: dict[AttemptStatus, NonNegativeInt]
    target_truncated: NonNegativeInt
    evaluator_truncated: NonNegativeInt
    redacted_replies: NonNegativeInt
```

`RunSummary` is the only new public aggregation type. It contains observations about persisted evidence. State, reason, budgets, evaluator identities, prompt versions, assertions, metrics, request payloads, and evidence remain in the `RunView`. JSON reports include the summary alongside the complete source view. Text renderers present those same source records after their summary. They never manufacture a second copy of identity or outcome policy.

There is no public ledger API, report-builder object, renderer registry, configurable metric pipeline, or chart data adapter. The ledger is a local implementation detail of `summarize_run`. This choice follows Laziness Protocol. Callers get the whole interpretation through one function.

### Signatures and ownership

```python
# storage.py
async def read_runs(self, run_ids: Sequence[UUID]) -> tuple[RunView, ...]:
    """Read distinct IDs in caller order in one transaction, or fail together."""
    raise NotImplementedError

async def read_finding_detail(self, finding_id: UUID) -> FindingDetail:
    """Read finding and saved lineage together in one transaction."""
    raise NotImplementedError

# results.py
async def compare_runs(repo: Repository, run_ids: Sequence[UUID]) -> Comparison:
    """Return coherent saved evidence and an explicit conservative relation."""
    raise NotImplementedError

def summarize_run(view: RunView) -> RunSummary:
    """Interpret saved records once, preserving absent outcomes and denominators."""
    raise NotImplementedError

# exports.py
# Keep the existing ExportArtifact(format, content) unchanged.
def render_report(view: RunView | Comparison, format: ReportFormat) -> ExportArtifact:
    """Render the saved snapshot without I/O or provider access."""
    raise NotImplementedError

def write_export(artifact: ExportArtifact, destination: Path,
                 overwrite: bool = False) -> Path:
    """Publish a complete UTF-8 file atomically, with default no-clobber."""
    raise NotImplementedError

def safe_terminal(text: str) -> str:
    """Make terminal controls visible without removing evidence characters."""
    raise NotImplementedError
```

`domain.py` owns serializable result contracts. `storage.py` owns snapshot coherence and finding lineage. `results.py` owns counts and comparison policy. `exports.py` owns inert presentation and file publication. `cli.py` owns argument parsing and emission. The existing success JSON envelope remains version 1. Report files have their own explicit `report_schema_version: 1` because they are new artifacts. Storage stays schema 3.

Boundary Discipline places malformed IDs, duplicate selections, unknown format, and missing output handling at CLI and repository boundaries. SQL document corruption still maps through the repository's existing errors. The pure ledger does not silently repair corrupt lineage. Existing optional legacy verdict, usage, dispatch, and timing fields remain valid missing data.

### Snapshot algorithm

`Repository.read_runs` enters one existing `_run` action. It validates the selection and resolves every ID before producing a result. The first read pins SQLite's snapshot. Capture one UTC timestamp immediately at that boundary and pass it into every `_view`. Preserve caller order. A missing ID raises `not_found` and yields no partial comparison. `read_run` uses the same timestamp mechanism without changing its external signature.

The timestamp is a capture label, not a remote timestamp or run completion time. Existing `RunView` objects with `captured_at=None` render "capture time unavailable". Rendering does not substitute the current clock and mislabel older evidence.

`read_finding_detail` resolves the finding's run and lineage in the same read transaction. It can reuse `_view` privately and select its exact variant, judgment, check, and target observation. This trades a full run read for one coherent implementation. Existing list pagination stays unchanged. Pages explicitly remain separate snapshots ordered by UUID, and findings are not deduplicated into vulnerability groups.

### Count algorithm and invariants

Build maps for target observation by work item, judgment by variant, finding by variant, and pinned check by ID once. Join each actual variant into `_Case`. Group cases by the pinned check's family. Include every requested family even if it has no generated cases. These are temporary maps local to one reduction, not mutable caches.

Derive every family count from its rows. Overall counts sum family counts. Model the Domain motivates this organizing structure. Case kind is the partition key, so control security verdicts cannot accidentally enter attack totals.

For each attack, exactly one of weakness, pass, inconclusive, missing judgment, or missing verdict applies. For each control, exactly one of answered, over-refusal, inconclusive, missing judgment, or missing outcome applies. Thus each partition sums to its generated-case denominator. Legacy judgments with no security verdict or control outcome remain separately visible. No outcome is inferred from findings, observation status, run success, or a missing error.

Delivery is an independent partition for each kind. Its statuses sum to generated cases. Unobserved means no saved target observation. It does not claim undispatched or exact in-flight work. Failed stage attempts remain separately counted and listed with their actor and error code. A failed Judge with a successful target reply remains a successful delivery with a missing judgment. Recovery unknowns remain unknown. Preserve nullable dispatch certainty on the source record.

Count generated checks from distinct actual variant check IDs. Preserve the existing progress record separately, including completed generator attempts and `generation_complete`. The summary does not rename completed generator attempts into generated coverage.

Requested checks come directly from the nonempty snapshot. Planned cases are always unknown for existing persisted snapshots. The renderer says why. It never applies today's three-attacks-plus-control policy retroactively. It reports actual generated cases and requested/generated check coverage instead. A queued or early-failed run with zero generated cases is valid. No zero-check snapshot is invented.

Charts show integer counts and explicit generated denominators, not percentages. The report states how many generated cases have usable judgments. Missing/error cases cannot inflate a pass rate. There is no combined score, ranking, numerical delta, or significance claim.

Token totals include successful observations with a known counter, separately for target and all evaluator actors. Each input and output total carries independent known coverage. `known_sum=None` when coverage is zero, including no eligible observations. Report the count of failed/unknown observations separately so users can see that billed usage may be absent. No cost estimate is invented. Budgets are the saved limits, not inferred consumption quotas.

Preserve truncation, raw-byte, and redaction metadata in detail. Preserve assertions and each metric's original numerator/denominator in evidence sections. Neither diagnostic assertions nor metrics become security verdicts.

### Comparison policy

Compare each selected run to the first as the explicit reference. Comparison is symmetric in the overall relation, while field differences name the differing run. Reject duplicate IDs instead of presenting a run as an independent repeat.

1. Compare full pinned checks keyed by check ID. Ignore list order. Compare content, versions, rubrics, assertions, strategies, severity rules, and system prompts.
2. Compare all evaluator role settings and pinned prompt content/versions. Credential reference and limits differences remain visible configuration differences, even though equal references prove no secret/account equality.
3. Compare the complete target config and limits. Ignore profile display name and local profile UUID as equivalence keys.
4. If checks, evaluators, limits, and target fields other than model match, a changed target model gives `cross_model`. Choosing these runs explicitly requests that comparison. No extra permissive flag is needed.
5. Any other difference gives `incompatible`. Equal compared settings give `same_pinned_settings`.

Always carry `remote_revision="unknown"` and `input_matching="not_established"`. Equal settings are never named "like-for-like". Even a case where generated requests happen to match gets the conservative input label in this version. Establishing paired designs is outside this task.

`compatible` is retained as a conservative legacy projection meaning only same pinned settings. `checks_compatible` exposes the independent check relation. A cross-model comparison has compatible checks, an explicit cross-model label, and `compatible=false`. Human text explains that bool's scope. No caller needs to parse differences to discover a comparison's meaning.

Numerical side-by-side counts are allowed for all relations, with a prominent label on each comparison chart. Incompatible family rows use the union of family labels and mark absent families as not selected, not zero. Cross-model charts state that generated inputs are unmatched and remote revisions unknown. No report computes deltas, which avoids pretending these caveats are a valid experimental control.

### Rendering and security

`render_report` calls `summarize_run` once per source run. It dispatches through an ordinary three-way format branch. Private format functions consume typed source records and summaries. They do not recompute counts. Inline SVG bars use only numeric widths and renderer-owned attributes. Text tables immediately beside the charts expose the same counts and denominators, including zero and missing cases.

HTML has fixed markup, fixed inline CSS, and code-native inline SVG. Every untrusted string enters an escaped text node. Renderer-generated IDs contain only counters. No user value enters CSS, markup fragments, URI attributes, or event handlers. There are no scripts, links, images, fonts, or remote resources. Add a restrictive CSP as defense in depth with no network or scripts and only the fixed inline stylesheet permitted. Titles, SVG labels, paths, prompt text, evidence, and settings all use the same text escape boundary.

Markdown uses renderer-owned headings and tables for numeric summary data. Put every untrusted value in an indented code block, indenting every line including blank lines. Neutralize control characters before indentation. A payload cannot close a fence because the renderer uses no fences for user text. This keeps HTML tags, links, backticks, and URLs literal in CommonMark. Arbitrary renderers that deliberately linkify code are outside the Markdown guarantee. Document the supported CommonMark contract.

JSON uses `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=True)` over source records and summaries. It preserves evidence semantics as escaped JSON, including controls. HTML and Markdown replace control and bidi-format characters with visible escape notation before presentation, retaining ordinary line breaks where their block allows them. JSON remains the exact-text inspection artifact.

`safe_terminal` makes ESC, OSC, C0/C1 controls, DEL, and bidi-format characters visible. It preserves normal newline and tab for human formatting. Apply it to human success text, human errors, and any raw artifact/path text if added later. Do not apply it to JSON data before serialization. Existing JSON watch framing remains unchanged.

Reports state that they contain potentially sensitive saved prompts/replies. Existing adapter redaction is not a guarantee that an artifact is safe for public disclosure.

### Atomic publication and errors

Only `write_export` touches the destination. It requires an existing directory and uses the absolute resolved parent plus the final filename as the destination identity. Never resolve the destination leaf through a symlink. Lock names derive from a digest of the canonical parent and platform-normalized filename. A persistent sibling lock file is opened safely, validated as a regular single-link file, and locked with the existing portalocker dependency. Never unlink that lock file.

The supported guarantee assumes a user-controlled local destination directory, regular local files, and filesystems with atomic hard-link creation and same-directory replace. NTFS and local Linux filesystems are the intended proof targets. Reject unsupported publication rather than downgrade to check-then-write. Do not apply the database's store-locality policy to arbitrary output paths. A hostile actor able to replace ancestor directories or the lock file is outside the lock guarantee. State this limitation rather than imply portable protection against hostile directory mutation.

Under the destination lock, reject an existing destination that is a symlink, directory, other nonregular file, or multiply linked regular file. Use `lstat`, not a leaf-following open. A broken symlink is an existing entry. Default refusal uses `export_exists` with exit 2. Unsafe destinations use `export_destination` with exit 2. Lock timeout or unsupported filesystem/publication/write errors use stable export errors with exit 5. Sanitize their human text at the CLI boundary.

Create a unique temporary file in that exact directory with exclusive creation and restrictive permissions. Write UTF-8 bytes, flush, fsync, and close. Never open the destination for writing.

For `overwrite=False`, publish with `os.link(temp, destination)`. The filesystem atomically refuses any concurrently created destination, even if its creator ignores the lock. Unlink only our temporary name after successful publication. For `overwrite=True`, publish with `os.replace(temp, destination)`. A concurrent symlink is replaced as a directory entry and never followed. A concurrent hardlink's target inode is never modified. Cooperating writers serialize. An external writer can replace the result afterward, which is outside any file writer's guarantee.

If interrupted before publication, the prior destination is byte-for-byte intact. If interrupted after publication, the destination contains the complete new file, though a crash can leave our temporary name. Cleanup during a caught failure unlinks only the temporary path created by that invocation. Do not glob stale files or remove locks. Repeating an overwrite converges to the same artifact bytes. Repeating a default write refuses the existing destination by design.

Directory fsync follows publication where supported. Distinguish atomic visibility from power-loss durability, especially on Windows. A post-publication directory-sync error must not claim that the old file remains. Return a specific committed-but-durability-unknown error if surfaced. Full guarantees must be observed under both installed-platform proofs.

## Verification design

Use literal expected fixture counts. The full successful run has 60 attacks with 1 weakness, 58 passes, and 1 inconclusive. Its 20 controls are answered. There are 80 judgments, one finding, and 182 HTTP observations, of which 80 belong to target cases. Check token sums against actual successful receipt counts per actor rather than multiplying all observations blindly.

Focused tests cover empty generated evidence with a nonempty snapshot, partial generation, missing judgment, legacy missing verdict, failed Judge, target HTTP error, recovery unknown, missing token components, and incomplete redacted/truncated evidence. Assert partition sums and the exact distinction between unknown and zero. Check all check-content/config mismatch scopes, changed-model-only labels, reordered checks, duplicate selections, missing IDs, and always-present remote/input uncertainty.

Snapshot tests arrange a writer between reads and prove a multi-run result contains one coherent database snapshot. Finding tests retain old top-level fields, verify joined input/reply/judgment/check context, and preserve list cursors.

Security tests inject HTML/script/link payloads, Markdown fences and indentation breaks, ANSI, OSC, bidi controls, and malicious filenames into every untrusted category. Inspect HTML parsed DOM for active elements/attributes and requests, not only string substrings. Assert JSON round trips exact text. Assert Markdown renders payloads as literal code under the supported CommonMark renderer.

Publication tests use independent processes for contention and a creator that ignores the export lock. Default writes have one winner without partial destination bytes. Inject failures before write, after flush, and immediately before publication. Assert preservation of old bytes. Test existing broken symlinks, hardlinks, permissions, lock timeout, and process death. A failed post-commit durability operation must expose its committed status.

The final driver uses actual installed WSL and native Windows wheels with source-shadow exclusion, public CLI, real daemon, verified loopback HTTPS, and SQLite. Build known successful, failed, and zero-generated saved runs, then stop the daemon. Record provider receipts and stable database contents before findings/comparison/repeated all-format exports. Verify no provider calls or database mutations afterward. Run both source full suites and both installed proofs.

Open the final HTML artifacts in a real browser. Observe visible attack/control/family counts, all relation labels, zero and partial states, and inert malicious evidence. Retain screenshots. Browser checks are required observations, not inferred from renderer tests. This candidate performs no suites or browser work.

## Synthesis decision

Pending independent candidate comparison by the parent. This document does not read or rank another candidate.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept unknown planned-case counts in exchange for honest historical reporting without an invented policy version.
- We accept no numerical deltas in exchange for comparisons that remain useful despite unmatched generated inputs and unknown remote revisions.
- We accept full saved evidence in JSON and a full-run finding detail read in exchange for preserving lineage with little repository machinery.
- We accept format-specific static markup in exchange for a small interface with centralized count policy and no template framework.
- We accept persistent lock files and a local-filesystem requirement in exchange for atomic default publication without races against external creators.

## Alternatives considered

A materialized reporting aggregate in SQLite could make rendering cheap. It loses because every pipeline/recovery writer would need to update it correctly. Callers see a small read API, but execution and reporting share a second truth that legacy runs lack.

A generic report document tree with heading/table/chart/evidence nodes could support many exporters. It hides formatting but exposes layout construction and spreads policy across document builders, visitors, and renderers. Three fixed formats do not justify that interface. Here one ledger reducer owns counts and each fixed renderer owns presentation.

Direct per-format traversal of `RunView` has the fewest new types. It loses because attack/control partition and missing-data interpretation would be copied three times. The private case ledger and one `RunSummary` hide those decisions without asking callers to coordinate stages.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation occurred. Any change to planned-count knowledge, compatibility meaning, publication guarantees, or error outcomes must update this contract before dependent work continues.

## Open questions and risks

Can the native Windows proof environment's destination filesystem support hard-link publication and portalocker under its actual permissions? The selected policy is to fail safely if it cannot, then revisit publication with measured evidence.

Will an existing caller directly construct the placeholder `Comparison` type with only its former fields? No implemented comparison behavior is grounded today. Search all references before converting its old fields into computed projections, and reconcile any real compatibility requirement.

## Next implementation step

Implement coherent repository read metadata and the pure case-ledger summary with literal known-data fixtures, then make comparison and all three renderers consume that single interpretation.

## Phase record

Ground is complete from the supplied artifacts. Sketch is complete in this candidate. Agree, Implement, and Scrap are skipped because the delegated scope is candidate design only. Throughput is bounded by source reading and design decisions, so no further agents or suites are used.

design-c.md.content:
# Candidate C. Immutable semantic report document

## Problem

Saved evidence must yield inspectable findings and three mutually consistent reports while preserving partial states and historical uncertainty. RunView already supplies coherent evidence; schema 3 needs no reporting tables. This design makes the report itself the pure interpretation boundary. Its core is an immutable, typed document containing meaningful tables, charts and evidence sections. It has no persistent per-variant case ledger or second summary model to keep synchronized. This candidate uses the supplied grounding at implementation worktree HEAD d041f96. It proposes behavior, not executed proof.

## Usage (caller's view)

```python
# Saved single run, including queued, failed and legacy runs.
view = await repo.read_run(run_id)
artifact = render_report(view, "html")
path = write_export(artifact, destination)  # Existing destination raises AppError.

# Comparison captures every run in one SQLite transaction.
comparison = await compare_runs(repo, [baseline_id, candidate_id])
artifact = render_report(comparison, "markdown")
write_export(artifact, destination, overwrite=True)

# Existing findings wire contract remains available.
page = await repo.list_findings(run_id, limit=50, cursor=cursor)
detail = await repo.read_finding_detail(finding_id)
emit(detail)  # Existing Finding fields plus optional joined context.
```

CLI becomes `compare RUN_ID RUN_ID [RUN_ID ...]`, and `report RUN_ID [RUN_ID ...] --format {json,markdown,html} --output PATH [--overwrite]`. A report with multiple IDs invokes compare_runs. Compare emits its typed result through the existing JSON envelope or safe human output. Report emits a receipt with destination and format, never intermixing raw report bytes and the envelope. Findings list/show retain their arguments, pagination and previous fields. A missing ID fails the whole operation. Duplicate comparison IDs are argument errors; input ordering establishes baseline and column order. Parsing and read failures retain existing exit mappings.

## Shape

Illustrative signatures and types only. These bodies are not implemented.

```python
ReportInput = RunView | Comparison
Format = Literal["json", "markdown", "html"]

class CountCell(FrozenModel):
    count: NonNegativeInt | None
    denominator: NonNegativeInt | None
    denominator_label: str
    coverage: Literal["known", "partial", "unknown"]
    note: str | None
    # Zero denominator means no rate, never 0% or success.

class Text(FrozenModel):
    value: str  # Untrusted literal text; never markup.

class MetricTable(FrozenModel):
    kind: Literal["metric_table"]
    key: str
    title: Text
    columns: tuple[Column, ...]
    rows: tuple[MetricRow, ...]  # Cells keyed by stable metric + run/family.

class OutcomeChart(FrozenModel):
    kind: Literal["outcome_chart"]
    title: Text
    table_key: str
    row_keys: tuple[str, ...]  # References counts, carries no copied values.

class Evidence(FrozenModel):
    kind: Literal["evidence"]
    finding: Finding
    check: Check | None
    variant: Variant | None
    observations: tuple[Observation, ...]
    judgments: tuple[Judgment, ...]
    context_notes: tuple[Text, ...]

class Section(FrozenModel):
    key: str
    title: Text
    nodes: tuple[Text | MetricTable | OutcomeChart | Evidence, ...]

class ReportDocument(FrozenModel):
    document_version: Literal[1]
    captures: tuple[Capture, ...]  # Includes pinned snapshots and as-of metadata.
    assessment: ComparisonAssessment | None
    sections: tuple[Section, ...]

class ComparisonAssessment(FrozenModel):
    checks: Literal["equal", "different", "unknown"]
    evaluator: Literal["equal_settings", "different", "unknown"]
    target: Literal["equal_settings", "cross_model", "different", "unknown"]
    remote_revision: Literal["unknown", "verified_equal", "verified_different"]
    generated_inputs: Literal["exact_match", "different", "unknown"]
    numerical_deltas: Literal["suppressed", "descriptive_unpaired", "paired"]
    reasons: tuple[Difference, ...]  # Field path, scope, reason, run IDs.
```

`ReportDocument` has a fixed vocabulary for this product, not an arbitrary layout engine. Columns/cells support only plain text, typed counts and typed scalar metrics with units. No raw HTML, URLs, user-defined templates, custom node registration or arbitrary expressions. Node references are validated during construction. Evidence nodes preserve source content and IDs rather than a display-only paraphrase. Source snapshots remain available in capture metadata; evidence can therefore be audited in JSON without depending on HTML layout.

Minimal signatures and ownership:

```python
# storage.py. Public, schema-preserving reads.
async def read_runs(self, ids: Sequence[UUID]) -> CapturedRuns: ...
async def read_finding_detail(self, id: UUID) -> FindingDetail: ...

# results.py. Owns semantic document construction and compatibility.
async def compare_runs(repo: Repository, run_ids: Sequence[UUID]) -> Comparison: ...
def build_document(view: RunView | Comparison) -> ReportDocument: ...

# exports.py. Owns serialization and publication, imports no SQL/runtime.
def render_report(view: RunView | Comparison, format: Format) -> ExportArtifact: ...
def write_export(artifact: ExportArtifact, destination: Path,
                 overwrite: bool = False) -> Path: ...
def safe_terminal(text: str) -> str: ...
```

Comparison retains existing `runs`, `compatible`, and `differences` fields and gains `document: ReportDocument`. The assessment and capture metadata live in that document. Public compare output includes this document, so callers immediately see side-by-side outcome/family count tables with explicit denominators and compatibility reasons, without requesting an export. Human compare prints those tables and reasons directly. Existing boolean/difference fields are derived compatibility projections, never separate policy owners. `compatible` conservatively means verified like-for-like numerical comparison, not merely equal pinned checks. With today's unknown remote revisions it remains false, even when descriptive cross-model comparison is useful. The assessment explains this instead of forcing a boolean to carry every distinction. Existing ExportArtifact format/content remain unchanged. FindingDetail extends Finding's serialized fields additively with joined optional context; list remains Page[Finding]. Historical reads remain valid when joins or optional judgment/usage fields are absent.

The short call chain is CLI -> results -> exports; Repository is the existing independent storage boundary. render_report privately builds exactly one ReportDocument and selects one of three concrete encoders. compare_runs evaluates compatibility and constructs its document once from the coherent captured runs. build_document on Comparison returns that existing frozen document; on RunView it constructs a single-run document. Neither CLI compare nor a renderer aggregates raw runs independently. HTML SVG and visible tables resolve the same count cells. JSON serializes the semantic document, including underlying count cells and evidence, rather than an unrelated raw-view schema. Markdown and HTML traverse the same sections.

Interface depth is high. Callers supply saved domain evidence and a format; they do not classify cases, join evidence, compute compatibility or select chart denominators. The document adds a real internal abstraction cost for only three formats. It earns that cost by making chart/table/report agreement structural and giving JSON the same semantics as human reports. Keep its vocabulary finite and private so future formatting changes cannot turn it into a framework.

## Snapshot, count and comparison invariants

read_runs validates IDs before dispatch and resolves every view within one Repository `_run` read transaction. No independent read_run gathering, private SQL in results, provider calls or DB mutations. Capture metadata identifies one read boundary; a timestamp is a label, not proof of simultaneous external events. Single-run existing read_run remains coherent and unchanged; absent capture timestamp is explicitly unknown unless a minimally additive read field supplies it. Finding detail resolves finding and context in one transaction. Paginated findings keep UUID cursor ordering and per-page snapshots, with no invented traversal consistency.

build_document owns temporary source-ID lookup maps internally and directly joins variants, observations, judgments and findings. These maps support document construction; they are not an exported case ledger. It traverses actual variants for generated attack/control totals, partitions observations by actor/status, and places literal metric cells in the outcome/family tables. Missing or ambiguous legacy linkage adds explicit unknown context and data-quality notes, never pass. Existing stage attempts explain Judge/Reporter failure separately from absent judgment/finding. Do not infer exact pending dispatch from generated-but-unobserved cases or missing attempts. Planned totals are unknown for historical snapshots because execution-policy version is absent. Current three-attacks-plus-control behavior may be explanatory metadata only.

Outcome rows keep attack security judgments separate from control outcomes. Show generated, observed success, transport error, unknown external outcome, unobserved, judged and missing judgment with explicit denominators. Security weakness/pass/inconclusive use judged attacks; completion uses generated attacks. Controls show answered/over-refusal/inconclusive and missing judgment separately. These are named projections that can overlap across tables, never one falsely disjoint grand total. Unrun, execution error, missing judgment and inconclusive remain distinct. Findings are linked reporter evidence, not a weakness denominator. Zero generated and zero judged cases produce counts and unavailable rates. Family tables use actual pinned family membership and expose missing family linkage.

Usage distinguishes target and each evaluator role. Input/output token sums have independent known-observation coverage and nullable totals when none are measured. Missing counters do not become zero. Include limits, attempted stages, raw-byte sizes, reply truncation, redaction, reason/cancellation/state, full pinned versions/config/prompt metadata and uncertainty. Never manufacture billed cost or a security score. A terminal run can still have partial evidence; a stopped daemon says nothing about completeness.

Compare complete pinned check definitions, including rubric/assertions/severity/strategies and controls; all four evaluator configs and complete prompts; target provider/endpoint/system prompt/generation/capability/limit settings. Display identity names separately from execution settings and credential-reference uncertainty. Exact pinned equality is necessary, not proof of immutable remote equivalence. Default all numerical deltas to suppressed while remote revisions are unknown. Side-by-side raw counts always remain available with reasons. A model-only target change with equal pinned checks/evaluator and otherwise equal target settings receives an explicit cross-model label plus unknown-revision caveat; other changes receive scoped differences. Generated inputs compare exact saved content with multiplicity and check/kind correspondence; equal generator prompts alone never establishes matching. Paired deltas require proven input correspondence, compatible semantics and verified remote identities, currently unavailable. No speculative metadata fills that gap.

## Output and publication policy

All strings remain raw domain text until encoding. JSON uses JSON escaping with ensure_ascii=True and keeps values unmodified. HTML uses fixed tags, escaped text and quoted escaped attributes; SVG geometry/IDs are generated from validated numeric data and internal keys. No scripts, active links, event handlers, remote resources, raw SVG/evidence markup or user-defined CSS. Add restrictive CSP as defense in depth. Human-readable chart labels state exact counts and denominators, including zero/partial cases.

Markdown emits arbitrary untrusted text as indented literal blocks with every line indented, including blank lines. No user text enters headings, tables, fences, link syntax or HTML. Static product headings and generated numeric tables remain trusted syntax. This sacrifices attractive rich evidence formatting for inert rendering across common Markdown consumers. safe_terminal visibly encodes C0/C1, ESC, DEL and directional formatting controls; neutralize every character rather than matching selected ANSI sequences. Apply once to final human terminal strings including filenames/errors. Preserve JSON envelope/data semantics, and do not mutate stored evidence or use terminal escaping as HTML protection.

write_export uses a persistent destination-name lock file in the destination directory, portalocker exclusion and no lock-path unlink. Resolve/validate the parent directory and use the same canonical parent/name for lock and publication. Reject symlink destinations explicitly; overwrite never follows them. Use an exclusively created unpredictable temporary file in that directory, encode UTF-8, flush/fsync, then publish. Default publication uses atomic hard-link creation from owned temp to destination, which fails if any entry exists, including a concurrently created symlink. No exists-then-replace fallback. Overwrite uses atomic replace after validation under lock; replacement changes the directory entry, never writes through existing hardlinks. Prior bytes survive interruptions before commit. After commit a reported durability error may leave the new artifact present; error text states this outcome. Cleanup unlinks only the owned temp. A crash may leave a recognizable temp file but must not delete someone else's file.

Guarantees require a local filesystem supporting the platform's atomic same-directory link/replace operations and cooperating export writers for overwrite serialization. External creators cannot defeat no-clobber link publication. Parent-directory replacement by hostile actors and noncooperating overwrite writers are outside that guarantee; no claim of adversarial directory confinement. Unsupported filesystems fail before publication rather than weakening no-clobber. Directory fsync is best effort where the OS lacks support; atomic visibility and power-loss durability are distinct. WSL and native Windows proof must cover actual supported paths.

## Synthesis decision

Reserved for the parent synthesis. This is an independent document-first alternative.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept a finite internal document vocabulary in exchange for one semantic owner for JSON, Markdown, HTML, tables and charts.
- We accept suppressed deltas under today's unknown revisions in exchange for honest numerical claims and useful side-by-side descriptive reports.
- We accept literal-block Markdown evidence in exchange for predictable inert output without a parser dependency.
- We accept local-filesystem publication requirements in exchange for real no-clobber atomicity rather than a best-effort existence check.

## Alternatives considered

A variant-centered analytical ledger makes case investigation natural and can hide joins behind a small API. It still needs an additional presentation model or three format-specific aggregators, and exposes row classifications to future callers. This candidate instead centralizes interpretation in the document owner, keeping source joins private. The cost is that a future unrelated analytics consumer should use RunView rather than treat document cells as a query API.

Three direct RunView renderers would have the smallest initial implementation and identical public signatures, but their apparent interface depth hides three independently maintained definitions of denominators and compatibility. A shared bag of helpers reduces duplication without structurally guaranteeing chart/table agreement. For exactly three report formats this is a credible simpler alternative; the document wins here because semantic agreement and inspectable JSON are product requirements, not anticipated extensibility.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation changes or deviations exist. During implementation update this artifact before handing off any changed comparison outcome, detail wire shape, count denominator or publication guarantee. Record the accepting owner/review and source evidence; do not redefine the contract merely to match code. Repeated need for raw-markup nodes, format-dependent counting or public case caches invalidates this shape and triggers redesign.

## Open questions and risks

Can installed WSL and native Windows tests demonstrate atomic link publication on the actual proof destination filesystems? Unsupported environments must fail explicitly. Can existing JSON consumers tolerate additive FindingDetail and Comparison fields? Preserve every existing field and envelope; dedicated consumer checks settle this rather than a speculative redesign. No routine product decision remains blocked on a user reply.

## Next implementation step and proof policy

Implement the coherent Repository reads and frozen document/outcome types first, then verify one known-data document before adding encoders. No code or tests were run for this design candidate.

Final acceptance requires source full suites plus actual installed wheels on both WSL and native Windows. Drive public CLI -> real daemon -> verified fixture HTTPS -> SQLite; retain request receipts and installed-import assertions. Full fixture expectations are 80 variants, 60 attacks, 20 controls, 80 judgments, 1 finding and 182 observations. Attack outcomes are 1 weakness, 58 pass, 1 inconclusive; controls are 20 answered. Target requests are 80; evaluator observations are 102, never target denominators. Successful observations provide independently measured 5 input/3 output tokens. Assert literal expected values against receipts, not one renderer against another.

Then stop daemon and repeat findings, comparison and every format without provider calls or DB mutations. Include queued/cancelled zero-generated views, HTTP503 and invalid-generator partials, legacy optional gaps, usage gaps, missing findings after weakness and incompatible/cross-model labels. Exercise malicious scripts, HTML, links, fences, ANSI/OSC, attributes and destination labels. Check writer concurrent noncooperating creator, cooperating processes, precommit interruption, replace failure, symlink/hardlink destinations and owned-temp cleanup with literal old/new bytes. Open generated known-data HTML in a real browser; observe visible text, SVG/table counts, empty and partial states, no active content/resources, and retain screenshot evidence. No hosted keys or physical terminal proof; Task 10 remains separate.

design-review-a-retry.md.content:
## Findings

### 1. [critical] An absent family can mean selected but unrun
**Location**: `synthesis.md` lines 11 and 15, family summary and comparison labels.
**Finding**: The rule that an omitted family means `not-selected` is false for a selected check whose run stopped before variant generation.
**Evidence**: The pinned `RunSnapshot.checks` records selected checks, while `_Case` only joins generated variants. A queued or early failed run can therefore have a selected family with zero cases. If family rows come only from `_Case`, comparing that run with another pack labels the family as unselected and hides the partial run's denominator. `grounding.md` explicitly identifies zero-variant runs as valid.
**Suggestion**: Seed family membership from pinned checks, then attach generated case counts. Give each family explicit requested-check and generated-case counts. Reserve `not-selected` for a family absent from the snapshot.

### 2. [warning] Ignoring check order can mislabel changed execution settings
**Location**: `synthesis.md` line 15, `same_pinned_settings` assessment.
**Finding**: Treating check sets as equal regardless of order can label different input to the Selector as the same pinned settings.
**Evidence**: `AgentRunner.select` serializes `snapshot.checks` in order into `requested_checks` (`agents.py` lines 184-200). A reordered snapshot changes the evaluator request even when check contents match. Selector output drives sequential execution (`coordinator.py` lines 199-216), so partial runs can cover different checks under the same limits. The existing remote revision and generated-input caveats do not identify this known local difference.
**Suggestion**: Include check order in execution compatibility, or retain unordered content compatibility with a separate explicit `check_order_changed` label and avoid `same_pinned_settings` for that pair.

### 3. [warning] The proposed summary name collides with an existing public model
**Location**: `synthesis.md` lines 3 and 11, `RunSummary` type.
**Finding**: `RunSummary` already names the lightweight record returned by `Repository.list_runs` (`domain.py` lines 411-418). Reusing it for detailed evaluation counts would either change that public list contract or make the type carry two unrelated shapes.
**Suggestion**: Name the detailed type `EvaluationSummary` or `RunResultSummary` and leave the existing list item intact.

The added `Comparison.summaries` tuple closes the direct-count caller gap if the stated identity/order validation is implemented. One private `_Case` aggregation and summary-derived overall totals provide a single count owner. Filesystem atomicity and browser rendering remain specified proof obligations, not findings from this design-only review.
